chunks: When the reckoning is over Satan will say: 'The promise that was made to you by God was indeed a true promise; but I went back on the promise I had made, for I had no power over you except to call you; and you responded to my call. So blame me not, but blame yourselves. Neither can I help you nor can you give me help. I disavow your having associated me earlier (with God). The punishment for those who are wicked is painful indeed.'
ai.seo_question: What does Satan say about his power over humans on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the transition from Satan's subtle invitation (da'wah) to human free will, emphasizing that his 'authority' was merely persuasive rather than coercive. It serves as a pivotal moment where Satan disavows his followers, illustrating the ultimate futility of those who associated partners with God (shirk) and reinforcing the concept of divine justice where each soul bears its own burden.
